legend: Busy Beaver has collected some pairs of seashells, and he is trying to make them into two beautiful bracelets!

He has N%%ZSMJ0%% pairs of seashells, where both seashells in the i%%ZSMJ1%%-th pair have type ai%%ZSMJ2%%. He wants to make two bracelets, such that each bracelet has one seashell from each pair. Busy Beaver decides his own metric for a beautiful pair of bracelets, which is minimizing the length of the longest common subsequence∗%%ZSMJ3%% between two bracelets.

Formally, let s%%ZSMJ4%% and t%%ZSMJ5%% be two permutations of the original array a%%ZSMJ6%%. We want to find (s,t)%%ZSMJ7%% that minimizes the length of the longest cyclic common subsequence, f(s,t)%%ZSMJ8%%, defined by the following:
Consider all cyclic shifts of array t%%ZSMJ9%%, denoted as t1,t2,…,tn%%ZSMJ10%%†%%ZSMJ11%%.
Let LCS(s,t)%%ZSMJ12%% be the length of the Longest Common Subsequence between s%%ZSMJ13%% and t%%ZSMJ14%%. Then f(s,t)=max1≤i≤nLCS(s,ti).%%ZSMJ15%%
Unfortunately, Busy Beaver has too many seashells to find the most beautiful bracelet pairs by hand. Please help him!

∗%%ZSMJ16%%An array s%%ZSMJ17%% is a subsequence of an array t%%ZSMJ18%% if s%%ZSMJ19%% can be obtained from t%%ZSMJ20%% by deleting some (possibly none or all) elements from t%%ZSMJ21%%, without reordering the remaining elements.
†%%ZSMJ22%%A cyclic shift ti%%ZSMJ23%% of an array t=[t(1),t(2),…,t(n)]%%ZSMJ24%% by i%%ZSMJ25%% places is given by [t(1+i),t(2+i),…,t(n+i)]%%ZSMJ26%%, where indices are taken modulo n%%ZSMJ27%%.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer T%%ZSMJ28%% (1≤T≤500)%%ZSMJ29%%, the number of test cases. The description of each test case follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single positive integer N%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤N≤500)%%ZSMJ31%%.
The second line of each test case contains N%%ZSMJ32%% integers a1,a2,…,aN%%ZSMJ33%% (1≤ai≤109)%%ZSMJ34%% — the types of seashells Busy Beaver has collected.
It is guaranteed that the sum of N%%ZSMJ35%% across all test cases does not exceed 500%%ZSMJ36%%.
output: For each test case, output two lines. The first line consists of N%%ZSMJ37%% integers s1,s2,…,sN%%ZSMJ38%%, and the second line consists of N%%ZSMJ39%% integers t1,t2,…,tN%%ZSMJ40%%, representing some (s,t)%%ZSMJ41%% that minimizes f(s,t)%%ZSMJ42%%.
If there are multiple solutions, print any of them.
note: Note that f([1,2,3],[1,3,2])%%ZSMJ43%% is 2%%ZSMJ44%% because LCS([1,2,3],[1,3,2])=2%%ZSMJ45%% ([1,2]%%ZSMJ46%% is a shared subsequence). This is the maximum LCS%%ZSMJ47%% over all cyclic shifts of t%%ZSMJ48%%:
